content.text: No change-of-control trigger exists anywhere, and the assignment clause is mutual with an M&A/affiliate carve-out. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Paragraph (h) gives AP exactly what the preferred position requires on the material terms: AP may assign without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent that may not be unreasonably withheld. There is no walk-away feature — no blanket prohibition on Customer assignment, and no deemed-assignment or change-of-control provision anywhere in the document (search for "change of control" returns nothing). The termination provision (p0016) is limited to expiry-of-term notice, material breach and insolvency, so Kubient has no right to terminate or re-price on an AP change of control. Two sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: the free-assignment carve-out is mutual (so Kubient may also assign to its own affiliate or acquirer without our consent, which is squarely the fallback position of a mutual right to assign to successors), and there is no express bar on Kubient assigning to an AP competitor. Neither is material enough to redline given the clause otherwise sits at or above the fallback.
